beats.title: Cato Records a Honey Cheesecake
beats.description: A Roman statesman's farming handbook set down a baked cake of cheese and flour finished with a coating of honey.
beats.note: De agri cultura, c. 160 BCE; an early detailed recipe, not the earliest honey cake

beats.title: Indians Crystallise Sugar
beats.description: Sugar makers in northern India learned to boil cane juice into hard crystals, the start of sugar as a keepable sweetener.

beats.title: Gingerbread Reaches Europe
beats.description: An Armenian monk is said to have taught French clergy to bake spiced honey bread, spreading the gingerbread tradition.
beats.note: Traditional date for Gregory of Nicopolis

beats.title: Nuremberg Lebkuchen Recorded
beats.description: A German city's spiced honey cakes appear in records, a festive treat that still bears the city's name.

beats.title: The Candy Cane Is Handed Out
beats.description: A choirmaster bent sugar sticks into shepherd's crooks to keep children quiet during a long church service.

beats.title: A Paris Cafe Serves Gelato
beats.description: A Sicilian entrepreneur opened a Paris coffeehouse that made frozen ices and ice cream fashionable.

beats.title: Baker's Chocolate Is Founded
beats.description: An Irish immigrant and a Massachusetts doctor began grinding cocoa beans in a mill that grew into a famous baking chocolate brand.

beats.title: Turkish Delight Goes on Sale
beats.description: An Istanbul confectioner opened a shop selling soft, gelled sweets dusted with sugar that won fans across Europe.

beats.title: The Sachertorte Is Invented
beats.description: A teenage apprentice improvised a dense chocolate cake with apricot jam for a prince's guests in Vienna.

beats.title: Fry's Makes the First Chocolate Bar
beats.description: A Bristol firm pressed cocoa butter, sugar and cocoa into a solid bar meant for eating rather than drinking.

beats.title: Cadbury Sells the Chocolate Box
beats.description: A British chocolatier packed bonbons in a decorated box, the first to be sold as a gift of sweets.

beats.title: The Chocolate Easter Egg Appears
beats.description: A Bristol chocolate maker began selling hollow eggs made of smooth eating chocolate for the spring holiday.

beats.title: Daniel Peter Makes Milk Chocolate
beats.description: A Swiss chocolatier mixed condensed milk into chocolate and created the smooth sweet bar the world came to love.

beats.title: Lindt Invents the Conche
beats.description: A Swiss chocolate maker's machine kneaded cocoa for hours, producing chocolate that melted smoothly in the mouth.

beats.title: Cracker Jack Debuts at the Fair
beats.description: Visitors to a Chicago world's fair tried a new treat of molasses-coated popcorn and peanuts.

beats.title: Jell-O Is Sold as a Dessert
beats.description: A New York cough-syrup maker's fruit-flavoured gelatin powder was named and sold as a wobbling dessert.

beats.title: Hershey's Milk Chocolate Bar
beats.description: A Pennsylvania caramel maker began mass-producing affordable milk chocolate bars for ordinary Americans.

beats.title: Ice Cream Cone at the St Louis Fair
beats.description: At a world's fair, a rolled waffle became a handy holder for scoops of ice cream and caught on across the country.

beats.title: Oreo Is Introduced
beats.description: A New York biscuit company launched a chocolate sandwich cookie with a cream filling that became a world favourite.

beats.title: Eskimo Pie Is Patented
beats.description: An Iowa shopkeeper coated ice cream in chocolate so it could be eaten by hand, creating the first ice cream bar.

beats.title: Haribo Makes the Gummy Bear
beats.description: A German confectioner shaped fruit-flavoured gelatin sweets like dancing bears, starting a chewy candy craze.

beats.title: Pavlova Is Created
beats.description: A meringue dessert with a crisp shell and soft centre, topped with cream and fruit, was named for a famous ballerina.
beats.note: Origin disputed between Australia and New Zealand; 1926 is the widely cited date

beats.title: The Mars Bar Is Launched
beats.description: A British factory began selling a bar of nougat and caramel coated in milk chocolate.

beats.title: Kit Kat Is Launched
beats.description: A York chocolate maker introduced a four-finger wafer bar originally sold as a snack for workers.

beats.title: The Chocolate Chip Cookie Is Baked
beats.description: An innkeeper in Massachusetts chopped up a chocolate bar into her cookie dough and invented an American favourite.
beats.note: Toll House Inn; some sources say 1930

beats.title: Marshmallow Peeps Are Mass-Produced
beats.description: A candy firm bought a small maker of sugar-coated marshmallow chicks and began turning out millions every spring.
beats.note: Just Born acquired the Rodda Candy Company in 1953

beats.title: Chupa Chups Lollipops Appear
beats.description: A Spanish confectioner put a stick in a ball of sweet candy so children could eat it without sticky fingers.

beats.title: Nutella Is Launched
beats.description: An Italian firm sold its chocolate and hazelnut spread in jars, later a breakfast favourite worldwide.

beats.title: Twix Arrives in the Shops
beats.description: A British chocolate company launched a biscuit and caramel bar sold in a twin pack coated in chocolate.

beats.title: Cadbury Creme Egg Is Named
beats.description: A chocolate shell filled with fondant resembling an egg white and yolk became a springtime sweet staple.
beats.note: Introduced 1963, sold under this name from 1971

beats.title: Kinder Surprise Hits the Shelves
beats.description: A hollow chocolate egg with a toy hidden inside went on sale from an Italian confectioner.

beats.title: Ben and Jerry Open Their Scoop Shop
beats.description: Two friends opened an ice cream parlour in a converted Vermont gas station and built a chunky-flavoured empire.

beats.title: Dippin' Dots Beads of Ice Cream
beats.description: A microbiologist froze ice cream into tiny beads using liquid nitrogen and sold it as a futuristic dessert.

beats.title: The Cronut Hits New York
beats.description: A SoHo bakery's croissant-doughnut hybrid sparked queues around the block and a global wave of pastry hybrids.
